key_insight: High-order IMEX BDF–FEM schemes achieve unconditional stability and optimal convergence for a regularized Hodgkin–Huxley model on branched axons, without timestep–mesh coupling.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient simulation of electrical pulse propagation and splitting in branched neural cables, with higher-order variants reducing runtime at tested accuracy targets.
method: Combine BDF orders 1–5 with conforming finite elements of any fixed degree p ≥ 1.
Smoothly mask extrapolated gates and apply a voltage cutoff to control conductances and gate rates.
Use one linear voltage solve per timestep, followed by independent nodal gate updates.
evidence_signal: Manufactured solutions recover predicted orders through BDF5–P4; action-potential simulations demonstrate propagation and splitting, and within-family work–precision tests show higher-order runtime gains.
watch_item: The guarantees concern the regularized model and require appropriate solution regularity and starting histories; numerical quadrature must meet the stated residual-defect condition to retain optimal convergence.
paper_title: High-Order Unconditionally Stable IMEX BDF--FEM Schemes for the Hodgkin--Huxley Model on a Branched Axon
